A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GQT research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite the shortened title, redesigned layout and expanded evaluation in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original GQT results on 18 node-classification datasets and component ablations on ogbn-arxiv and Minesweeper, including Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on 22 benchmarks, component ablations, adversarial attacks, tokenizer comparisons and inference efficiency, including Appendix E.

M1.justification: The GNN/RVQ tokenizer, DGI and GraphMAE2 objectives, commitment loss, codebook updates, semantic-edge/PPR construction, token modulation and Transformer pooling are retained. The new pseudocode principally documents existing mechanisms. Full-graph serialization is clarified in Appendix D; concatenating node tokens for graph-level input was already described in v1 Section 3.

E1.justification: v2 adds Peptides-Func graph classification, Peptides-Struct graph regression, COCO-SP inductive node classification and PCQM-Contact link prediction, extending the original node-classification evaluation into molecular and image-derived graph tasks. It also introduces adversarially perturbed PubMed and ogbn-arxiv scenarios while retaining the original 18 datasets.

E2.justification: v2 introduces direct comparisons with a reconstruction-trained RQ-VAE tokenizer for robustness and downstream prediction (Tables 5 and 9), substantially extending the comparison beyond GNN/Transformer predictors. Graph-Mamba joins the new long-range comparison, and GAT becomes an inference-efficiency comparator. Comparator membership in the original benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce LRGB splits and AP, MAE, macro-F1 and MRR metrics, GR-BCD/PR-BCD attack testing, and full-node inference time and GPU-memory measurements. Appendix D also expands the stated codebook-size search to include 2048 and 4096. Because v1 already mentions using 4096 on ogbn-products, this documentation change does not establish rerunning the existing experiments. Attack budgets remain unspecified.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ogbn-arxiv and Minesweeper component ablations, v2 adds adversarial robustness analysis, a reconstruction-only tokenizer comparison testing the value of multi-task self-supervision, and measured inference-efficiency comparisons (Section 6.2 and Appendices E.2–E.3). These address substantive questions previously unsupported by dedicated experiments.

E5.justification: The original ablation tables report single values; their v2 counterparts, Tables 6 and 8, add ± uncertainty throughout. Main benchmark reporting already used five-run means with ± values in v1. The PDFs do not establish increased run counts for the ablations or specify what their new uncertainty terms represent.

E6.justification: v2 adds long-range, attack, RQ-VAE and efficiency results and revises existing benchmark and ablation entries. For example, Computer changes from 92.05±0.16 to 93.37±0.44 and Photo from 95.35±0.18 to 95.73±0.18, now exceeding VCR-Graphormer's 95.53. The new PCQM-Contact comparison favors Exphormer, 0.3587 versus GQT's 0.3427. Minesweeper changes from 95.28 to 97.36 in the main comparison but remains 95.28 in v2 Tables 8–9. These are revised reported results, not established same-configuration gains.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematical formulation is retained, without new theorems, proofs, formal assumptions or guarantees. The GAT and PPR equations move from the main text to Appendix A. The added tokenizer/RVQ pseudocode supplies procedural documentation rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion change the headline claim from state-of-the-art performance on 16/18 benchmarks to 20/22 and explicitly include long-range benchmarks. The central contributions—decoupled self-supervised tokenization, hierarchical quantization and token modulation—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 attributes improved attack robustness to multi-task self-supervision and explicitly treats downstream prediction as a proxy for generalization. Appendix E.3 newly qualifies memory savings as occurring after tokenizer training, whose GNN still processes original features, and interprets measured inference speed as comparable to sparse GAT. Existing component-level interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link, tokenizer/RVQ pseudocode and Table 7's selected configurations for every dataset, substantially extending v1's search ranges and framework/hardware descriptions. These disclosures improve reproducibility information, although the pseudocode contains inconsistencies: Algorithm 2 replaces a vector residual with its squared norm and initializes codebooks randomly despite the retained K-means description.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds VQ-GNN and additional vector-quantization applications in point clouds, proteins and molecules. New references support the long-range benchmarks, attacks, Graph-Mamba comparison and graph-foundation-model discussion. The central positioning as a learned graph tokenizer remains stable; duplicate-reference consolidation and publication updates are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and condenses the introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion. It shortens the title, adds descriptive serialization/modulation subheadings, moves GAT/PPR explanations into an appendix and reorganizes the appendices around preliminaries, model details, datasets, settings and additional results. These changes extend beyond inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different visual template, including a boxed title/abstract, new heading and citation styling, and wider text and table layouts. It adds five tables and two algorithm displays, rearranges retained tables and reformats Figure 1 while preserving its central pipeline.

improvement.justification: v2 closes an important evidence gap: v1 suggested applicability beyond node classification, whereas v2 actually evaluates graph classification, regression and link prediction alongside inductive node classification. Measured inference costs, explicit limits on memory savings, selected configurations and ablation uncertainty further strengthen assessability. Unexplained Minesweeper discrepancies, unspecified attack budgets and faulty new pseudocode limit reliability, but the broader task evidence and improved resource accounting provide a substantial net improvement.
